tagline: Around the upper Lamprey, by farmland and Antique Alley.
intro: Off NH 101 the loop runs roughly with the upper Lamprey River, which rises in Meadow Lake in Northwood and flows south through Deerfield. It takes in Northwood, a town of lakes and antique shops along its Antique Alley, then Deerfield and Candia, through rolling farmland and past the old centers of each town.
Candia was first called Charmingfare, likely for its bridle paths. It was renamed for the island, Crete by its other name, where Governor Benning Wentworth had once been held prisoner.

moments.title: Northwood
moments.text: When the Portsmouth to Concord Turnpike came through around 1800, the town's taverns took in sledge and stage passengers, and later shoe factories took the place of five of its sawmills.

moments.title: Deerfield
moments.text: On the hilltop common of Deerfield Parade, beside the old postal road between Concord and Portsmouth, the militia drilled and paraded in the Revolution and again in the Civil War.

moments.title: Candia
moments.text: Candia Village once ran a water-powered complex of mills, and the old Portsmouth railroad bed through town is now the Rockingham Recreational Trail.
